slides.heading: Copying Lists Safely
slides.body: Copying Lists Safely is part of List Operations and Methods. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Copying Lists Safely
slides.body: copy() creates a separate list with the same items. This helps avoid changing the original list by accident.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Copying a list safely is like photocopying a document before writing notes on it.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Copy a list, add a new item to the copy, then print the original.
slides.hint: Use copy = original.copy() before appending to copy.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Make a safe copy of scores, append 100 to the copy, and print both lists.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
